prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1320; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the policyholder's driver describing a side impact at a signalized intersection. The claimant reports a concussion and is now represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Requested the scene photographs and the statements of the two independent witnesses.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who gave the same sequence of events as the policyholder. Both vehicles had the right-of-way questions addressed by the signal phase noted in the report.

Entry 4: Photos from the vehicle inspection show damage to the driver's side door and quarter panel consistent with the reported angle of impact. The estimate will be reviewed against the photographs.

Entry 5: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the loss date. No issues with the policy terms were found.

Entry 6: Reviewed the vehicle's prior repair history and found no earlier damage to the same panels. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 7: Counsel's letter arrived requesting medical authorizations. Forwarded the request to the claims file and noted the claimant's account has been consistent across every contact so far.

Entry 8: Received the initial medical records showing a concussion diagnosis. Records do not indicate any prior injury to the head or neck area.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury. Requested updated records and a treating physician summary to understand the course of care.

Entry 10: Reviewed the medical file with the claims supervisor. Whether the concussion was caused by this collision has not yet been determined, and the file remains open pending further medical review.

Entry 11: Spoke with counsel's office to confirm receipt of the requested records and to advise that the medical causation review is ongoing.

Entry 12: Scheduled a follow-up with the claims supervisor to review the outstanding medical records and set the next action date for the bodily injury evaluation.
